literal: Emperor Shenwu, Part Two
idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu, Part Two

literal: In the first year of Tianping, on renchen of the first month, Shenwu campaigned west against the Feiyetou barbarian Qidouling Yili west of the River, destroyed him, and relocated his tribe to Hedong.
idiomatic: In Tianping 1 (534), on renchen day of the first month, Gao Huan marched west against Qidouling Yili of the Feiyetou beyond the River, destroyed him, and resettled his people in Hedong.

literal: In the second month, the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple suffered calamity.
idiomatic: In the second month the nine-story pagoda of Yongning Temple burned.

literal: Then a man came from Donglai and reported that people along the coast had all seen it in the sea; shortly mist rose and it vanished.
idiomatic: Soon a traveler from Donglai reported that people all along the coast had seen it in the sea; then mist rose and it disappeared.

literal: Interpreters held heaven's intent seemed to say: Yongning suffers calamity, Wei shall know no peace;
idiomatic: Commentators read heaven's message thus: Yongning burns, and Wei will know no peace;

literal: It flew east into the sea — Bohai shall answer.
idiomatic: it flew east into the sea, and Bohai shall answer.

literal: The Wei Emperor already harbored a divergent plan. Attending Minister Feng Longzhi spoke privately with Sun Teng — Longzhi had lost his wife, and the emperor wished to give him his sister in marriage.
idiomatic: The Eastern Wei emperor already nursed secret designs. Attending Minister Feng Longzhi spoke privately with Sun Teng; Longzhi's wife had died, and the emperor wished to give him his sister in marriage.

literal: Teng also did not fully believe it, but resented Longzhi in his heart and leaked the words to Husi Chun.
idiomatic: Sun Teng did not wholly believe it, but resented Longzhi and betrayed the conversation to Husi Chun.

literal: Chun reported it to the Wei Emperor.
idiomatic: Husi Chun reported it to the emperor.

literal: Also Sun Teng entered the palace precinct with weapons and on his own authority killed a censor.
idiomatic: Sun Teng had also entered the palace precinct armed and killed a censor on his own authority.

literal: Both fled and came to surrender.
idiomatic: Both fled north to Gao Huan.

literal: They reported that the Wei Emperor had beaten Attendant Liang Xu before the court, and Vice Director of the Imperial Household Yuan Zigan swung his arm and struck him, saying to Teng: "Tell your King of Gao that the Yuan family's fist is just like this.
idiomatic: They reported that the emperor had beaten Attendant Liang Xu before the court and that Vice Director of the Imperial Household Yuan Zigan had struck the emperor, telling Sun Teng, "Tell your King of Gao that a Yuan fist is just like this.

literal: " Campaign Commander-in-Chief Lou Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Campaign Commander-in-Chief Lou Zhao pleaded illness and returned to Jinyang.

literal: The Wei Emperor thereupon made Husi Chun acting Campaign Commander-in-Chief, assigning supervisory generals and governors of Henan and Guanxi provinces.
idiomatic: The emperor thereupon appointed Husi Chun acting campaign commander-in-chief and posted supervisory generals and governors across Henan and the Guanxi region.

literal: Prince Huashan Zhi was at Xuzhou; Shenwu sent Di Zhen to seize his keys of command.
idiomatic: Prince Huashan Zhi was holding Xuzhou; Gao Huan sent Di Zhen to strip him of command.

literal: Han Xian, Inspector of Jian Province, and Cai Jun, Inspector of Ji Province, were both of Shenwu's sworn fellowship, and the Wei Emperor resented them.
idiomatic: Han Xian of Jian Province and Cai Jun of Ji Province had sworn fellowship with Gao Huan, and the emperor resented them.

literal: Therefore he abolished Jian Province to remove Xian, sent Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun to investigate Jun's crimes, and made Palace Opener Jia Xianzhi Inspector of Ji.
idiomatic: He abolished Jian Province to remove Han Xian, sent Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun to investigate Cai Jun, and appointed Palace Opener Jia Xianzhi inspector of Ji.

literal: Jun refused; the Wei Emperor grew angrier still.
idiomatic: Cai Jun refused, and the emperor's anger only mounted.

literal: In the fifth month an edict was issued, saying he would campaign against Gou Wu, mobilizing troops from Henan provinces, augmenting the palace guard, and holding the River Bridge.
idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict announced a campaign against Wu, mobilizing troops from the Henan provinces, strengthening the palace guard, and guarding the River Bridge.

literal: On dingsi in the sixth month, the Wei Emperor secretly edicted Shenwu: "Yuwen Heitai, since pacifying Qin and Long, has demanded undue shares; should he turn treacherous, affairs would require strategy.
idiomatic: On dingsi in the sixth month the emperor secretly wrote Gao Huan: "Since Yuwen Heitai pacified Qin and Long he has demanded ever more; should he play false, the matter will require deliberate handling.

literal: But his memorials had not fully turned defiant, and a forward campaign would be hastily rushed — therefore he summoned the ministers to debate whether it could be done.
idiomatic: But his memorials have not yet turned outright defiant, and a swift advance would be rash—I have summoned the ministers to weigh the matter.

literal: All said to feign a southern campaign, alert within and without — first to guard against Heitai's unexpected move, second to overawe Wu and Chu.
idiomatic: All said to feign a southern campaign and put the realm on alert—first to guard against Heitai's surprises, second to overawe Wu and Chu.

literal: " At this time the Wei Emperor intended to campaign against Shenwu; Shenwu had deployed commanders, and fearing suspicion, there was this edict.
idiomatic: At the time the emperor was preparing to move against Gao Huan; Gao Huan had already deployed commanders and, fearing suspicion, prompted this edict.

literal: Shenwu then memorialized: "Jing Province adjoins the barbarian south and lies close to the capital domain; Guan and Long rely on distance and harbor rebellious designs.
idiomatic: Gao Huan memorialized in reply: "Jing Province borders the barbarian south and lies close to the capital; Guan and Long, trusting in their distance, are plotting rebellion.

literal: Your servant now secretly marshals thirty thousand troops, intending to cross from Hedong;
idiomatic: I have quietly mustered thirty thousand troops and plan to cross from Hedong;

literal: Also sent Heng Province Inspector Kudiligan, Ying Province Inspector Guo Qiong, Fen Province Inspector Helü Jin, and former Wuwei General Peng Le with forty thousand troops to cross at Laiwei Ford;
idiomatic: I have dispatched Kudiligan of Heng Province, Guo Qiong of Ying, Helü Jin of Fen, and former Wuwei General Peng Le with forty thousand to cross at Laiwei Ford;

literal: Sent Campaign Commander Lou Zhao, Xiang Province Inspector Dou Tai, former Ying Inspector Yao Xiong, and Bing Province Inspector Gao Longzhi with fifty thousand to strike Jing Province;
idiomatic: Campaign Commander Lou Zhao, Xiang Inspector Dou Tai, former Ying Inspector Yao Xiong, and Bing Inspector Gao Longzhi with fifty thousand to strike Jing Province;

literal: Sent Ji Province Inspector Wei Jing, former Ji Inspector Gao Aocao, Ji Province Inspector Cai Jun, and former Attending Minister Feng Longzhi with seventy thousand Shandong troops and fifty thousand shock cavalry to campaign on the Jiang Left.
idiomatic: Wei Jing of Ji, former Ji Inspector Gao Aocao, Ji Inspector Cai Jun, and former Attending Minister Feng Longzhi with seventy thousand eastern troops and fifty thousand shock cavalry to campaign on the Jiang Left.

literal: All are pledged to their commands, awaiting orders in concealment.
idiomatic: All await hidden orders from my command.

literal: " The Wei Emperor perceived the change, produced Shenwu's memorial, ordered the officials to debate it, and wished to halt Shenwu's armies.
idiomatic: The emperor saw through the shift, produced Gao Huan's memorial, ordered the court to debate it, and sought to halt all his armies.

literal: Shenwu then gathered the provincial staff, had them debate broadly, and reported back by memorial.
idiomatic: Gao Huan summoned his provincial staff, had them debate the matter at length, and reported back by memorial.

literal: Again by oath he declared his loyalty: "Your servant was set apart by favored sycophants; Your Majesty suddenly granted suspicion — the crime of raising rebellion was settled in Erzhu times.
idiomatic: He also pledged his loyalty with an oath: "Favored sycophants have set Your Majesty against me; the charge of rebellion was settled when the Erzhu were destroyed.

literal: If your servant does not exhaust loyalty to the utmost, daring to fail Your Majesty, may my body suffer heaven's calamity and my descendants be extinguished.
idiomatic: If I am not utterly loyal and fail Your Majesty, may heaven punish my body and cut off my line.

literal: If Your Majesty will extend trust to this loyal heart and leave weapons unmoved, one or two sycophant ministers I would ask be weighed and removed.
idiomatic: If Your Majesty will trust my loyal heart and keep swords sheathed, I ask that one or two sycophants be weighed and dismissed.

literal: " On xinwei the Emperor again recorded the opinions of civil and military officials at the capital to reply to Shenwu, ordering Attendant Wen Zisheng to draft the edict.
idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor recorded the opinions of officials at the capital to answer Gao Huan and ordered Attendant Wen Zisheng to draft the reply.

literal: Zisheng hesitated and dared not write; the Emperor leaned on a camp chair, drew his sword, and turned stern.
idiomatic: Zisheng hesitated, afraid to write; the emperor gripped his folding chair, drew his sword, and darkened his face.

literal: Zisheng then drafted the edict thus:
idiomatic: Zisheng then drafted the edict:

literal: Earlier I sent my heartfelt blood afar to show the King, deeply hoping we would understand each other — yet wicked men sat idle and bred division.
idiomatic: I sent you my heartfelt pledge from afar, hoping we might understand each other—but wicked men have bred division between us.

literal: Recently Sun Teng hastened thither in urgency, causing hearers to suspect some divergent plot — therefore I sent Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun to set forth my mind fully.
idiomatic: Sun Teng's recent flight has made men suspect conspiracy, so I sent Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun to make my mind plain.

literal: Now receiving the King's memorial, words and oath earnest and moving — turning it over in thought, I am still not fully clear.
idiomatic: Your memorial is earnest and moving, yet the more I turn it over the less I understand.

literal: With my slight person, meeting the King's martial strategy, without laboring a blade's inch I sat as Son of Heaven — as the saying goes, those who gave me life are my parents, those who honored me are the King of Gao.
idiomatic: By your martial power this slight person became emperor without drawing a blade—as men say, my parents gave me life, and the King of Gao gave me the throne.

literal: Now if without cause I turn against the King.
idiomatic: If I now turn against you without cause,

literal: Plotting mutual attack — let my body and descendants answer as in the King's oath.
idiomatic: and plot war against you, let my body and line pay as your oath foretold.

literal: Heaven and Earth bear witness to these words.
idiomatic: Heaven and Earth bear witness.

literal: Recently, fearing Yuwen would rebel and Helü Sheng respond, I gathered for alert, wishing to support the King jointly.
idiomatic: Fearing Yuwen's rebellion and Helü Sheng's response, I ordered alert and meant to support you.

literal: Today Yuwen's envoys succeed one another; observing his conduct, there is no further sign of divergence.
idiomatic: Yuwen's envoys come and go without pause, and I see no sign of treachery.

literal: Helü Sheng in the south opens borderlands and renders merit to the state — considered, there is nothing to blame.
idiomatic: Helü Sheng in the south has opened the frontier and served the state—on reflection, nothing warrants blame.

literal: If the Lord wishes separate campaigns, with what words shall it be justified?
idiomatic: If you wish to march separately, what pretext can you offer?

literal: The southeast has not submitted — long the case; since former courts it has been placed beyond reckoning.
idiomatic: The southeast has long withheld submission, and former courts put it beyond reckoning.

literal: Today the realm's registered households are halved — it is not fitting to exhaust troops to the utmost in warfare.
idiomatic: Registered households are half what they were—the realm cannot bear endless war.

literal: I am myself dim and obscure — I know not who the sycophants are; list their names and let me know.
idiomatic: I am myself dim—I do not know which men you mean; name them that I may know.

literal: As heard, Kudiligan told the King: "Originally one wished to take a weakling as lord; the King for nothing established this elder sovereign, making him hard to drive — now make a fifteen-day journey and he can be deposed, another established.
idiomatic: I hear Kudiligan told you, "We meant to put a weakling on the throne; you for nothing raised this elder emperor so he cannot be controlled—march fifteen days and he can be deposed and another set up.

literal: " Such talk is plainly a meritorious man of the King's circle — how could it come from a sycophant's mouth?
idiomatic: Such talk comes from your own chief followers—how could it come from a sycophant's mouth?

literal: Last year Feng Longzhi rebelled; this year Sun Teng fled — neither punished nor surrendered — who does not wonder at the King!
idiomatic: Feng Longzhi rebelled last year and Sun Teng fled this year—you neither punish nor surrender them—who does not wonder at you!

literal: Teng was the source of calamity yet shows no shame or fear; if the King serves his lord with full loyalty, why not behead and deliver both heads?
idiomatic: Teng began the trouble yet feels no shame—if you are wholly loyal, why not send me both their heads?

literal: Though the King opened plans to go west, four routes advance together — some wish to cross south at Luoyang, some to press east on the Jiang Left — those who speak must wonder at themselves; those who hear, how can they not suspect?
idiomatic: Though you speak of marching west, four columns advance together—some toward Luoyang, some toward the Jiang Left. Even the speakers must find it strange; how can hearers not suspect?

literal: If the King keeps loyalty without duplicity and rests quietly in the north, though here there be a million host, in the end there will be no thought of scheming against him.
idiomatic: If you keep faith and rest quietly in the north, though I have a million men I shall never plot against you.

literal: If the King abandons trust, embraces wickedness, and raises banners south — though not a horse or wheel remain, I would still wish to strike with empty fists and fight to death.
idiomatic: If you cast faith aside and march south, though not a horse or wheel remain to me I would still fight with empty fists to the death.

literal: I by nature lack virtue; the King already established me — the common people are ignorant and may say it was fitting.
idiomatic: I lack virtue myself; you raised me to the throne, and ignorant common folk may say it was fitting.

literal: If plotted against by others, my wickedness would be shown; even if the King kills me in turn, disgraced and ground to dust, utterly without regret.
idiomatic: If another plots against me, my wickedness is exposed; and if you kill me, disgraced and broken, I shall have no regret.

literal: Why?
idiomatic: Why?

literal: The King was first promoted by virtue, raised by righteousness — in one morning to turn against virtue and abandon righteousness is to have blame find its place.
idiomatic: You raised me by virtue and righteousness—to turn against both in a morning is to place blame where it belongs.

literal: Originally I hoped lord and minister one body, as if matched seals — I never imagined today we would be estranged to this point.
idiomatic: I hoped we would be as one, matched like seal halves—I never thought we would come to this estrangement.

literal: An old saying runs: "If a Yue man shoots me, I laugh and tell of it;
idiomatic: An old saying runs, "If a man of Yue shoots me, I laugh and speak of it;

literal: if my elder brother shoots me, I weep and tell of it.
idiomatic: if my elder brother shoots me, I weep and speak of it.

literal: " I am close to the King as kin, feeling as brothers — therefore I cast aside the brush and beat my breast, unawares weeping.
idiomatic: You are kin to me, my feeling toward you like a brother's—writing this I cast down my brush and beat my breast and weep without knowing it.

literal: Earlier, when Shenwu was about to go north from the capital, he held that Luoyang had long suffered ruin and disorder, royal vapor exhausted — though it had mountains and rivers for strength, the land was narrow and cramped, inferior to Ye; he requested relocation of the capital.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan was leaving the capital for the north he judged that Luoyang, long ravaged by war, had exhausted its royal aura; though fortified by river and mountain its lands were cramped—and Ye was better. He asked to move the capital.

literal: The Wei Emperor said: "Great Ancestor established the tripod at He-Luo as foundation forever; institutions were planned and completed only under Emperor Shizong.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Great Ancestor established the throne at He-Luo as an everlasting foundation; its institutions were completed only under Emperor Shizong.

literal: The King's merit lies in the altars of soil and grain — he should follow the Tahe precedents.
idiomatic: Your merit lies in the altars of state—you should follow the Tahe precedents.

literal: " Shenwu accepted the edict; at this time he again plotted it.
idiomatic: Gao Huan obeyed; now he raised the plan again.

literal: He sent three thousand cavalry to garrison Jianxing, augmented Hedong and Ji troops, at Baigou seized boats and forbade passage toward Luo, and had grain purchased and transported from the provinces into Ye.
idiomatic: He posted three thousand horsemen at Jianxing, reinforced Hedong and Ji, seized boats at Baigou and barred passage toward Luoyang, and had the provinces buy and ship grain into Ye.

literal: The Wei Emperor again edicted Shenwu: "If the King wishes to quiet human sentiment and cut off public talk, he need only return Hedong's troops, dismiss Jianxing's garrison, send Xiang Province's grain, recall Ji's army, have Cai Jun relieved, send Di Zhen out of Xu, halt weapons and disperse horses, each returning to household affairs.
idiomatic: The emperor wrote again: "If you wish to quiet rumor and end suspicion, return Hedong's troops, dismiss the Jianxing garrison, send Xiang Province's grain, recall Ji's army, replace Cai Jun, withdraw Di Zhen from Xu, sheathe swords and disperse horses, and let each man return home.

literal: If grain stores are needed, send transport separately — then slanderers will seal their tongues and doubt and regret will not arise.
idiomatic: If you need grain, send it separately—then slanderers will fall silent and doubt will vanish.

literal: The King may rest at ease in Taiyuan; I will rule with folded hands at Jing-Luo — in the end we will not lift foot to cross the river and point weapons at each other.
idiomatic: You may rest easy in Taiyuan; I shall rule at Luoyang—we shall never cross the river against each other.

literal: If the King turns his horse's head south and asks the weight of the tripod, though I lack martial prowess and wish to stop but cannot, I must for the altars and ancestral temple devise a death-defying stratagem.
idiomatic: If you turn south to contest the throne, though I am no warrior and wish to stop, I cannot—I must for altar and temple stake my life.

literal: The decision lies with the King — not something I can settle; stopping a mountain one basket short — let us pity each other.
idiomatic: The choice is yours, not mine—to stop a mountain one basket short of completion, let us pity what we lose.

literal: " At the time the Wei Emperor had Ren Xiang as acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with Palace Opener rank; Xiang abandoned office and fled to Hebei, holding a commandery to await Shenwu.
idiomatic: Meanwhile Ren Xiang, acting Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with Palace Opener rank, abandoned his post, fled to Hebei, and held a commandery awaiting Gao Huan.

literal: The Wei Emperor then edicted civil and military officials who came north to choose stay or go, issued an edict listing Shenwu's crimes, and prepared a northern campaign.
idiomatic: The emperor ordered northern officials to choose stay or go, published an indictment of Gao Huan, and prepared for northern campaign.

literal: Shenwu also reined horse and proclaimed: "I met the Erzhu's usurpation of power, raised great righteousness throughout the four seas, and bore up the sovereign — righteousness piercing dark and light.
idiomatic: Gao Huan reined in his horse and proclaimed, "When the Erzhu usurped power I raised righteousness throughout the realm and set the sovereign on the throne—righteousness binding dark and light.

literal: Wantonly slandered and framed by Husi Chun, my loyal integrity is made head of rebellion.
idiomatic: Husi Chun has slandered me and made loyalty into treason.

literal: Formerly Zhao Yang raised the hosts of Jinyang and executed the wicked beside the lord — today's southward march is only to execute Chun.
idiomatic: Once Zhao Yang raised the hosts of Jinyang to purge evil beside the throne—today's march south is only to purge Husi Chun.

literal: " He made Gao Ao vanguard, saying: "Had we taken the Minister of Works' counsel, how could there be today's move!
idiomatic: He made Gao Aocao vanguard, saying, "Had we followed the Minister of Works, we would never have come to this!

literal: " Sima Ziru answered Shenwu: "Originally one wished to set up the lesser — it was just for this."
idiomatic: Sima Ziru answered Gao Huan, "We meant to put a lesser man on the throne—this is exactly why."

literal: The Wei Emperor mobilized troops in Guanxi, summoned Helü Sheng to the mobile court, sent Grand Eastern Headquarters Changsun Chengye, Grand Commander Prince of Yingchuan Binzhi, and Husi Chun jointly to hold Wulao, Prince of Ruyang Xian to hold Shiji, Eastern Headquarters Chief Changsun Ziyan leading former Hengnong Administrator Yuan Honglue to hold Shan, and Jia Xianzhi leading Yu Province Inspector Husi Yuanshou against Cai Jun.
idiomatic: The emperor mobilized Guanxi, summoned Helü Sheng to the mobile court, posted Grand Eastern Headquarters Changsun Chengye, Grand Commander Prince Yingchuan Binzhi, and Husi Chun at Wulao, Prince Ruyang Xian at Shiji, Eastern Headquarters chief Changsun Ziyan with former Hengnong Administrator Yuan Honglue at Shan, and Jia Xianzhi with Yu Inspector Husi Yuanshou against Cai Jun.

literal: Shenwu sent Dou Tai and Left Wing Grand Commander Modou Lou Daiwen against Xianzhi, Han Xian against Xian.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Dou Tai and Left Wing Grand Commander Modou Lou Daiwen against Jia Xianzhi, and Han Xian against Prince Xian.

literal: Yuanshou's army surrendered.
idiomatic: Husi Yuanshou's force surrendered.

literal: Tai, Daiwen, and Xianzhi met at Changshou Ford; Xianzhi secretly agreed to surrender and led the army to withdraw.
idiomatic: Dou Tai and Daiwen met Jia Xianzhi at Changshou Ford; Xianzhi secretly agreed to surrender and withdrew his troops.

literal: Army Administrator Yuan Xuan perceived it and raced back.
idiomatic: Army Administrator Yuan Xuan noticed and raced back.

literal: He requested reinforcements.
idiomatic: He asked for reinforcements.

literal: The Wei Emperor sent Grand Commander Hou Jinshao to go to them.
idiomatic: The emperor sent Grand Commander Hou Jinshao to his aid.

literal: They fought east of Huatai; Xianzhi surrendered with his army and Shao died.
idiomatic: They fought east of Huatai; Jia Xianzhi surrendered with his army and Hou Jinshao was killed.

literal: In the seventh month the Wei Emperor personally led the great host to encamp at the River Bridge.
idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor personally led a great host to the River Bridge.

literal: Shenwu reaching more than ten li into Hebei, again sent messengers orally declaring loyal intent; the Wei Emperor did not reply.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, reaching south of the River, sent envoys again to declare his loyalty; the emperor did not answer.

literal: Shenwu then led the army across the river.
idiomatic: Gao Huan then crossed the river with his army.

literal: The Wei Emperor asked counsel of the ministers — some said to rely on Helü Sheng in the south, some said to go west to Guanzhong, some said to hold Luokou and fight to the death.
idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers: some said to join Helü Sheng in the south, some to flee west to Guanzhong, some to hold Luokou and fight to the death.

literal: No decision was reached.
idiomatic: No decision was reached.

literal: Meanwhile Yuan Binzhi and Husi Chun struggled for power without harmony; Binzhi abandoned Chun and returned directly, deceiving the Emperor: "Shenwu's troops have arrived.
idiomatic: Yuan Binzhi and Husi Chun quarreled for power; Binzhi abandoned Chun and rode straight back, telling the emperor falsely, "Gao Huan's army has arrived.

literal: " That same day the Wei Emperor withdrew to Chang'an.
idiomatic: That same day the emperor withdrew to Chang'an.

literal: On jiyou Shenwu entered Luoyang and lodged at Yongning Temple.
idiomatic: On jiyou Gao Huan entered Luoyang and lodged at Yongning Temple.

literal: On jiayin in the eighth month he summoned the hundred officials and said: "As ministers serving a lord, rescuing peril and disorder — if at leisure one does not remonstrate, in departure one does not accompany, at ease then dallying for favor and striving for glory, in urgency then fleeing — where lies the minister's integrity?
idiomatic: On jiayin in the eighth month he summoned the officials and said, "As ministers serving a sovereign, to rescue peril and disorder—if in quiet you do not remonstrate, in crisis you do not attend, at ease you scramble for favor and glory, in danger you flee—where is ministerial integrity?
